official.application_cycle: MOPGA 2027 - tenth call for applications; applications open 15 September 2026 and successful fellows arrive in France between September and December 2027
official.status_note: Applications opened 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026. Results are notified May-June 2027 and successful applicants arrive in France between September and December 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official page states that host laboratories receive no funding and that 'the fellowship is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses'; no tuition fee support is mentioned.

Status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF)
Fellowship paid directly by Campus France
A research stay agreement signed between the French host institution and the researcher
eligibility: Hold a doctoral degree awarded less than five years before the application deadline, i.e. have defended your PhD thesis between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive
Be exclusively of foreign nationality (all nationalities are eligible except French nationality)
Apply for the purpose of undertaking international mobility to France
Not be residing and professionally active in France at the time of application
Not have previously received a MOPGA fellowship
requirements: Applications must be submitted online through the Campus France SMApply platform; applications sent by email will not be considered
A research stay agreement must be signed between the host institution in France and the researcher
By supporting an application, host laboratories undertake to provide an appropriate scientific environment for the research stay, but receive no funding under the programme

This French Government fellowship cannot be combined with a French employment contract, such as a research contract or postdoctoral contract, or with any other individual funding awarded by a French government entity
The research project must fall within one of the five MOPGA research areas
documents: CV including a list of publications (4 pages max.)
Doctoral degree certificate (or official proof of degree)
CV of the scientific supervisor at the host laboratory (2 pages max.)

Letter of support from the scientific supervisor, co-signed by the laboratory director or accompanied by a letter of commitment from the laboratory director, confirming that the scientific environment and resources required will be made available and that the project is consistent with the laboratory's objectives
Copy of passport or national identity document
selection_criteria: Two-stage selection: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space assess the applications, then a scientific committee makes the final selection of the MOPGA 2027 fellows
Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies in the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process
coverage: Each fellowship includes, exclusively: a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500
Health coverage: health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance, followed by supplementary health insurance once registered with the French social security system
International travel costs to France are not covered; the host laboratory may be able to help but receives no funding from the programme
application_method: Agree the research project with a host laboratory in France and obtain the laboratory director's commitment

Prepare the research project description: project title, 6 keywords, summary (max. 2,000 characters), background and motivation (max. 2,000), scientific objectives (max. 2,000), methodology and timeline (max. 4,500), relevance to MOPGA (max. 2,000), and international collaboration/expected impact (max. 2,000)
Collect the required documents, including the supervisor CV and the co-signed support letter
Submit the application online via https://campusfrance.smapply.io/prog/mopga_2027/ before 15 December 2026
official.application_route: Online only, through the Campus France SMApply platform (applications sent by email will not be considered)
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be exclusively of foreign nationality (all nationalities except French are eligible) and must not be residing and professionally active in France at the time of application
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is designed for foreign researchers: all nationalities are eligible except French nationality, and applicants must be applying for international mobility to France
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The project must fall within one of five research areas: Earth system sciences; climate change and sustainability sciences; energy transition; societal challenges related to environmental issues; human, animal and environmental health under the One Health approach (only projects with a genuine integrated One Health dimension qualify - projects focused solely on medicine or human health are not eligible)
official.research_requirement: Applicants must define a research project to be carried out in a French host laboratory, described in eight sections: project title; 6 keywords; research project summary (max. 2,000 characters); background and motivation (max. 2,000); scientific objectives (max. 2,000); methodology and timeline (max. 4,500); relevance of the project to the MOPGA initiative (max. 2,000); international collaboration and/or expected impact for the applicant's country of residence or country of origin (max. 2,000). Applications may be submitted in English or French.
official.description: MOPGA (Make Our Planet Great Again) is a French Government visiting fellowship programme funded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) in partnership with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space (MESRE) and implemented by Campus France. Its tenth call for applications enables young international researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory, strengthening scientific contributions to the issues addressed at the Conferences of the Parties (COPs) under the Paris Agreement.
official.program_type: Government research fellowship (visiting fellowship for early career researchers)
official.english_requirement: Applications may be submitted in English or French; no IELTS/TOEFL score requirement is published

verification.notes: Monthly allowance (EUR 2,500), EUR 500 settling-in allowance, 12-month non-renewable duration, deadline 15 December 2026, eligibility rules, required documents, selection process and the non-coverage of travel all read directly from the official Campus France MOPGA 2027 page (updated 15 September 2026), which also confirms the SMApply application route.

applicant_utility.summary: MOPGA 2027 pays EUR 2,500 per month for 12 months plus a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, but it deliberately leaves tuition, relocation and international travel to the fellow, so treat it as living-cost support rather than full funding. The real first gate is the host laboratory: the application must rest on a signed research stay agreement with a French lab, so start lab outreach months before the 15 December 2026 deadline. Fellows are not employees - the award cannot be combined with any French employment contract or other French government individual funding, which rules out holding a French postdoc contract alongside it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-French researchers who defended their PhD between December 2021 and December 2026, are not resident and professionally active in France, and can secure a French host laboratory committed to a climate or environmental research project.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a host laboratory early and obtain the supervisor's support letter co-signed by the laboratory director (or a separate director's commitment letter) well before 15 December 2026
Verify the PhD defence date falls within December 2021 - December 2026 and gather an official proof of defence if the degree certificate is not yet issued
Draft all eight research-project sections and respect the character limits (methodology and timeline up to 4,500 characters; other sections up to 2,000)
Build a 4-page CV with publications, a supervisor CV within 2 pages, and line up 1-3 recommendation letters
Register and submit on the SMApply portal early - email submissions are rejected and no late route exists
common_rejection_risks: Being resident and professionally active in France at application, or holding French nationality
A PhD defended outside December 2021 - December 2026 (a defence after December 2026 is explicitly ineligible)
A project outside the five research areas, or a One Health submission without a genuine integrated environmental/animal dimension
A host laboratory commitment letter missing the laboratory director's co-signature or commitment letter
Budgeting as if travel or tuition were funded and arriving unable to cover relocation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel to France (explicitly not covered), any costs associated with the host laboratory (labs receive no programme funding), plus any living expenses beyond the EUR 2,500 monthly allowance and EUR 500 settling-in allowance.
document_audit: CV must not exceed 4 pages and the supervisor CV 2 pages - oversized files are a compliance risk
The support letter must be co-signed by the laboratory director or accompanied by the director's own letter of commitment
If the doctoral degree certificate has not been issued, an official certificate confirming the defence, proof of thesis submission, or another official institutional document is required
Recommendation letters: at least 1 and at most 3 - zero or four does not meet the published rule
A passport or national identity document copy is required - check validity well ahead of the September-December 2027 arrival
alerts: Hard deadline 15 December 2026 with the SMApply portal as the only submission route; email applications are not considered
Results only arrive May-June 2027 and fellows arrive September-December 2027, so plan visa timing and your current position's handover accordingly
The eligibility window may be extended by 18 months per child or by the actual duration of maternity leave, but the supporting documents must be included in the application file
The fellowship cannot be combined with a French employment contract (research or postdoctoral contract) or any other individual funding from a French government entity
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Campus France SMApply portal, complete the eight research-project sections, upload the CV, degree proof, supervisor CV, co-signed support letter, 1-3 recommendation letters and passport copy, then submit online before 15 December 2026.

The work sits inside the Digital Twin of France and its Territories (JUNN) project, initiated and co-led by IGN, Cerema and Inria, at the Centre Inria d'Universite Cote d'Azur (TITANE team) in Sophia Antipolis.
official.research_requirement: The PhD candidate will (i) develop efficient methods for detecting 3D changes and expressing them with simple geometric shapes, and (ii) analyse the spatio-temporal distribution of these geometric changes at large scales (from city districts to the entire country), working with airborne LidarHD campaigns and satellite-based Digital Surface Models.

The post is a 3-year fixed-term doctoral contract with a gross monthly salary of EUR 2,300, starting 1 December 2026 in Sophia Antipolis.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salaried 3-year doctoral contract at Inria's Centre Inria d'Universite Cote d'Azur (TITANE team, Sophia Antipolis), paying a gross EUR 2,300 per month for work on 3D change detection at national scale within the JUNN Digital Twin of France and its Territories project. Because it is employment rather than a scholarship, the gross figure is pre-deduction and French labour, social security and HR rules apply - budget on the net amount. Candidates need a graduate degree with a strong 3D geometry, computer vision and machine learning background plus C/C++ and Python programming skills and fluent English. Note the posting's ZRR warning: the post is likely situated in a restricted area, and an unfavourable Ministerial decision on access would cancel the appointment.
